utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just one or two preliminary matters before the witness is called. The first has to do with the time for the Prosecution's case. Mr. Groome, the Trial Chamber is concerned about the time that you have requested, an hour and a half, this for a witness whose evidence is to be confined to rebuttal. I've looked at the history of the times that you have requested, and there has been significant changes. First two hours in March, then in April three hours, then on the 9th of June the Trial Chamber issued its order concerning alibi evidence of this witness. A time of three hours was set. Then on the 17th of July, no doubt in response to the realisation that this witness's evidence would be confined to alibi testimony, the Prosecution indicated a half an hour for this witness. That was the final witness list. But a couple days ago on the list for this week, we see an hour and a half. Now, this witness, as I have said, is to give evidence in rebuttal of the alibi defence, and we don't see why an hour and a half should be needed. We intend to be very strict, because any evidence that you lead the Defence will have a right to respond to it. The evidence must be confined to -- to alibi, and you will have to persuade us as to why an hour and a half is needed. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The -- Mr. Vasiljevic testified for eight days, I believe in excess of 21 hours, 500 pages of transcript. In my attempt to deal with him most expeditiously, and I do apologise for the different time estimates, what I've done is the following, Your Honour: I have prepared a sheet which has the excerpts that the Prosecution wishes to rely on. It is but a small, small portion of the entire testimony, and, Your Honour, in the Vasiljevic judgement the Trial Chamber credited some of what Mr. Vasiljevic said and discredited some of what he said, and it seemed to me that you have the same task before you, and it also seemed to me that one of the tools that Judges use in assessing credibility is their impressions and their view of a witness as that witness gives their evidence. How long do they take to answer questions, you know, and their general appearance. So I have prepared the video excerpts. I have put them all together, and that takes precisely one hour and 28 minutes, and that is all of the evidence that the Prosecution wishes to rely on. It was my belief that by allowing the Chamber to see Mr. Vasiljevic testify and give his evidence related to the alibi in this case, the Chamber would be the optimal position to ask question of Mr. Vasiljevic, as well as the Defence would be in a good position to cross-examine him, and that would be all that -- Your Honour, that I would be seeking to do. I have but two or three other questions to put to him. I am relying on what he has given in sworn evidence prior to today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So you're saying that the evidence consists substantially of video excerpts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, we are not inclined to watch videos for an hour and a half. The witness is here. If you have questions for him, then put the questions to him. You should be selective in the videos that you wish to present to the Trial Chamber, but we don't see the need to watch an hour and a half or an hour and 20 minutes of videos with just two or three questions being put to the witness. We don't need more than half an hour, 40 minutes, to observe a witness to be able to assess his demeanour. The Chamber will grant you one hour for the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Before the witness is brought in may I raise two other -- or two preliminary matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, good afternoon. My name is Vladimir Domazet, Mitar Vasiljevic's counsel in these proceedings. I'd like to tell you that I talked to him yesterday for quite a long time in the detention unit, and he requested, and I'm sure he'll make that request here personally; namely, he's very worried about his testimony, about testifying, which could inflict damage on his family in view of the many people that are mentioned during his testimony should he be asked about them, and he asked that he be heard in private session. Now, since all the other -- because it's too late for any other protective measures. Beforehand he did not discuss this with the Prosecution, nor was he informed that he would be a witness. The first time he heard of that was when the Defence counsel came to visit him and conveyed that to him. So he did not have an opportunity to discuss any possible protective measures or what he is insisting upon now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you're seeking the protective measure of a private session. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, the Chamber, of course, would in the circumstances grant the private session, but I listened to you very carefully, and I noted that but for the time factor, Mr. Vasiljevic would have sought greater protective measures, and I'd like to know what those are, because the Chamber is sensitive to the -- the position that he finds himself in, and if it is at all possible to make arrangements for any additional measures we would consider doing so. MR. DOMAZET [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that this -- that a private session would suffice. It's quite enough. When I spoke about previous requests, that was, well, with other protective measures, a pseudonym and so on, but I think at this point in time that is no longer necessary. So if you grant a private session, that will be enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Domazet. Very well. We grant the private session, and we note that you have said that that is enough. Call the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm just wondering, in light of your granting of protective measures, would it be prudent to ask the director not to show that -- have a shot that shows Mr. Vasiljevic in the courtroom in case that compromises his security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, the court deputy will see to that. Court started late this afternoon, and I neglected to say why we were late. We were late because one of our members sat in another case this morning, and it should be on record that the Judges of this Tribunal make a tremendous sacrifice when they sit in two cases in one day. They finish one case at 1.45 and must begin the next at 2.15. That leaves very little time for consultation, which we do, and that's why we started late and I wanted the record to show that. Let's go back to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 11th day of September, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.16 p.m.,
